label.spicy: "Updating the pricing model now. I've built it on the standard discount, which puts the headline at £412k — the renegotiated rate would take it to £377k. Unless you say otherwise before 4 I'll go with standard and flag the assumption on the slide."
label.boardroom: "I am updating the pricing model on the standard discount, which produces a headline of £412k; the renegotiated rate would produce £377k. Absent a response before 4pm I will proceed on the standard basis and note the assumption on the slide."

consequence.spicy: She reads that between meetings and replies with one word. You were never blocked, the work moved, and she now knows you understand what the number does.
consequence.boardroom: This can be answered between meetings with a single word. The work was never blocked, and it demonstrates that you understand the implications of the figure.

label.spicy: "Quick one — is Renwick on standard discount or the renegotiated rate?"
label.boardroom: "Is this client on the standard discount or the renegotiated rate?"

consequence.spicy: Specific and answerable, which puts it well ahead of most. It just stops the work until she surfaces, and it doesn't show that you know why it matters.
consequence.boardroom: Specific and answerable, which is better than most. It nonetheless halts progress until she responds, and does not convey that you understand why the distinction matters.

label.spicy: "Hi — got a sec to talk me through the pricing model?"
label.boardroom: "Do you have a moment to talk me through the pricing model?"

consequence.spicy: You've asked for an unknown amount of her time to answer a question you haven't stated. She'll assume you understand less than you do, because you've given her nothing that says otherwise.
consequence.boardroom: This requests an undefined amount of time for an unstated question. It will be read as less understanding than you actually have, because nothing in it demonstrates otherwise.

label.spicy: Build it both ways and send both versions Thursday morning
label.boardroom: Prepare both versions and present them on Thursday morning

consequence.spicy: Twice the work, and you've handed the decision back to her at the worst possible moment. Two numbers on a Thursday morning is not thoroughness, it's an unmade decision in a nicer outfit.
consequence.boardroom: This doubles the work and returns the decision to her at the least convenient point. Presenting two figures on the morning of the meeting is an unresolved decision rather than thoroughness.
